Cascade: provide sample dataset and traffic profile (by 2025-06-14)
action_items: Owner: Priya Kapoor; Item: Prepare sample OpenAI-compatible SDK examples (JS + Python); Due: 2025-06-12
Owner: Ethan Brooks; Item: Provide 2 weeks of request logs and latency histogram; Due: 2025-06-14

header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE); Marta Lopez (Cascade Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (Cascade Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Cascade PM), Anya Tsai (Cascade Security)
summary: POC scoping call to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and integration approach. Customer wants an OpenAI-compatible integration for chat/structured outputs, tool/function calling for internal systems, and clear lat/throughput targets. Action items include sharing SDK examples, sample dataset, benchmark timeline, and compliance docs.
topics: Success criteria and metrics (p95 latency, throughput, cost)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes, quick intros?
[00:08] Marta (Cascade): hi i'm marta, head of ml at cascade, we own recommender and conversational assistant initiatives
[00:13] Ethan (Cascade): ethan here, platform eng, i'll own infra and bench metrics
[00:18] Samir (Cascade): samir, product, i'll be measuring success from user impact side
[00:22] Jordan (Redwood): great, priya and liam from our side, priya will do the deep integration bits. quick agenda: success criteria, traffic sizing, bench plan, integration approach (SDK / openai-compat), tool calling, next steps
[02:05] Priya (Redwood SE): ok jumping in on success criteria — what are your must-haves? we typically see p95 latency targets, throughput baseline and cost per 1M tokens as business metric
[02:22] Marta (Cascade): p95 less than 350ms for short-chat (prompt+response ~300 tokens), throughput initially 50 reqs/sec, scale to 200 reqs/sec during sales events, cost target is hard but we want to show 30-40% savings vs current eval of gpt-4o in hosted mode
[03:01] Ethan (Cascade): also data residency: eu only for EU customers, and we need audit logs and KMS integration for keys
[03:20] Anya (Cascade Security): SOC2 is required, plus SSO/SAML for console, RBAC is a must
[04:00] Priya (Redwood): that's all doable; for residency we can route requests to EU region and Dedicated or Private deployments can be provisioned. SOC2 is in our compliance pack, we'll share the doc. regarding p95 — depends on model choice and quantization; we'd recommend a medium-latency variant for this POC to hit 300-350ms
[05:12] Marta (Cascade): cool — on integration we want minimal changes to our existing stack, ideally an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and SDKs in JS/Python. also need function/tool calling to trigger internal inventory lookup and structured JSON outputs for our product pages
[05:40] Liam (Redwood): yep we expose OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints and SDKs; function calling is supported, though we have a couple of caveats about streaming + structured output that we'll document. for example, streaming events for partial structured payloads can be noisy, but we offer structured-output enforcement and schema validation during generation
[06:05] Samir (Cascade): can you enforce the JSON schema or do we need to post-parse?
[06:12] Priya (Redwood): we can do both. we have optional server-side schema enforcement feature where the runtime will reject non-conforming responses — useful for production. for POC, many customers do local validation first and then enable server-side enforcement in pilot
[07:00] Jordan (Redwood): let's talk workload sizing — ethan, can you share your expected RPS and token distribution?
[07:12] Ethan (Cascade): sure, baseline 50 rps, average prompt 120 tokens, response 220 tokens, 80% of calls are short chat for product q&a, 20% are longer full page generation (2k tokens). concurrency spikes up to 200 rps for promos
[07:40] Priya (Redwood): ok that distribution suggests we should benchmark both the short-chat optimized model and a larger context model; caching and prefix kv cache will help for repeated prompts, and batching helps cost savings for high throughput bursts
[08:12] Marta (Cascade): what about real-world bench? how do we measure parity vs openai/others? we want to run quality checks as well as perf
[08:27] Liam (Redwood): common approach: we run a dual-run benchmark — one against Redwood on a chosen model/quantization and one against your current baseline (OpenAI/Anthropic). metrics: latency (p50/p95), throughput, token cost, and quality via the eval set (ROUGE/semantic similarity and manual QA). we can host the bench or run it in your env if you want private data kept on-prem
[09:05] Ethan (Cascade): prefer us to run it in our VPC for data privacy; can you provide an on-prem agent or a private deployment package?
[09:18] Priya (Redwood): yes we have Private deployment packages and a VPC private control plane — for POC we can also do a short-lived dedicated pool in eu-west to mirror production; will share options and tradeoffs
[10:00] Samir (Cascade): timeline wise we want a 6-week pilot: week 0-1 onboarding/sample data, week 2 bench, week 3 analyze + tweaks, week 4 pilot traffic ramp, week 5 quality validation, week 6 decision meeting. is that feasible?
[10:25] Jordan (Redwood): that looks reasonable. our typical POC is 4-8 weeks; for eu-private + bench we can meet that 6-week timeline. we'll need sample data and a small dev account set up
[11:00] Marta (Cascade): ok, integration: how intrusive are SDK changes? we have an internal adapter to OpenAI — minimal if you support openai-compat endpoints
[11:20] Priya (Redwood): openai-compat is low-friction. we provide examples: passing function schemas, tool metadata, and structured-output schema. minor mapping for any non-standard headers. also support both REST and websocket streaming for client-side UX
[12:40] Ethan (Cascade): tool calling: we need the model to call an inventory-check tool and then return a structured object like {sku, available, etas}. how do you secure tool endpoints?
[12:58] Liam (Redwood): tool endpoints are proxied through a secure, authenticated connector. we can enforce mTLS and short-lived tokens; the callout is executed inside your VPC for private deployments. in hosted mode we proxy but provide customizable allowlists and auditing
[13:35] Anya (Cascade): that proxy approach needs detailed audit logs — who called what and with what payloads. also mask PII in logs
[13:48] Priya (Redwood): we redact full PII by default in the logs and provide configurable redaction policies. audit logs contain function name, call time, and status but payload redaction can be tuned
[14:20] Jordan (Redwood): pricing and pilots — we'll outline both a hosted bench option (fastest) and dedicated/private option (for residency and security) with estimated token costs and a reserved capacity price for the duration of the POC
[15:05] Marta (Cascade): what's the expected cost delta versus openai for similar throughput? a rough number helps sell internally
[15:18] Jordan (Redwood): rough ballpark: 20-40% lower per-token cost for optimized open models and quantized variants; if you need strict parity in quality we might pick a larger model where savings are lower but still meaningful; we'll put concrete examples in the pricing doc
[16:00] Ethan (Cascade): on benchmarks, what infra do you need from our side? we'll provide logs and an endpoint to send traffic from our load generator
[16:12] Priya (Redwood): ideally: a sample of requests (1000-10k), a small eval set for quality, and a staging endpoint or creds for private deployment. we'll provide runner scripts (JS/Python) and config for your load generator
[17:00] Samir (Cascade): quality metrics — we want both automated similarity and a small human eval (50-100 cases). can you help run the human eval?
[17:18] Liam (Redwood): yes we can support curation and manual scoring; often customers do a joint review session
[18:00] Marta (Cascade): any gotchas about structured output? we've had hallucinations where the JSON shape was wrong
[18:12] Priya (Redwood): things to watch: enforce strict schema, use function calling where possible (it helps reduce hallucination), and run a decoder-check step. server-side schema enforcement helps prevent malformed outputs from reaching users
[19:05] Anya (Cascade): security question: key management — can we use our KMS and HSM?
[19:20] Jordan (Redwood): yes, for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM; for Hosted we integrate with customer KMS via key wrapping or we can use our managed keys with additional contractual controls
[20:15] Ethan (Cascade): ok that's fine. about monitoring: do you provide token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards?
[20:30] Priya (Redwood): yes Redwood Console provides per-route, per-model dashboards, token-level cost, traces, and can emit logs to your SIEM via syslog or stream to S3. retention tiers are configurable
[21:00] Jordan (Redwood): let's outline the bench plan: 1) Redwood provides SDK + runner 2) Cascade supplies traffic/profile and eval set 3) Run short-run bench for both short-chat model and large-context model 4) Collect p50/p95, throughput, and quality metrics 5) Joint review — target week of 6/23
[24:00] Marta (Cascade): will you be able to show both streaming latency and final token costs in the report?
[24:12] Liam (Redwood): yes, streaming latency and tokenized cost per request included, plus recommended config (batching, kv cache, quantization) to meet your p95 target
[25:30] Samir (Cascade): integration question: can we keep our existing OpenAI adapter and switch endpoints via a feature flag?
[25:40] Priya (Redwood): absolutely, many customers do a feature-flagged swap; we'll give you the exact headers and responses to map.
[27:00] Ethan (Cascade): about function calling and partial failures — if the tool fails, what's the recommended fallback?
[27:12] Priya (Redwood): recommended pattern: return a structured error object and fallback to cached inventory or degrade to read-only info. we can wire automatic retries with backoff and circuit breaker at the SDK layer
[29:00] Jordan (Redwood): ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners
[29:12] Jordan (Redwood): Priya will send OpenAI-compat SDK examples (js/python) and runner scripts; jordan will send pricing for dedicated pilot; ethan will provide traffic logs and sample requests; anya to confirm compliance scope
[30:05] Marta (Cascade): sounds good. one ask — include a short code snippet showing function schema for inventory check in the doc
[30:18] Priya (Redwood): noted, will include in the SDK pack
[31:00] Samir (Cascade): any risk items? vendor lock-in concerns and long onboarding time are on our side
[31:12] Jordan (Redwood): we keep things portable — openai-compat reduces lock-in and we support model export policies for private deployments
[32:00] Marta (Cascade): ok final Q: who will be the point of contact for daily comms during the POC?
[32:10] Ethan (Cascade): i'll be the technical lead; samir for product decisions
[32:20] Jordan (Redwood): we'll put a shared slack channel and weekly syncs; propose Tuesday 10am UTC for weekly check-ins starting 2025-06-17
[33:00] Anya (Cascade): one more on logs retention — we may want 12 months for audit, can you support that?
[33:18] Priya (Redwood): yes configurable retention tiers up to multi-year, though long retention for hosted may require add-on
[34:00] Jordan (Redwood): alright we'll follow up with the docs and pricing; thanks everyone
[34:12] Marta (Cascade): thanks, talk soon
[34:20] (call ends)
